subject: FRANK -> ClayCode control/effect closure
frank_derived_assumption: FRANK requires recurrent control flow plus external capability/effect authority boundaries.
shared_ancestry_collapse: FRANK, Harness, GWT, ClayGraph and UnifiedDB project materials share ancestry and are not treated as independent replication.

independent_checks.finding: structured block/loop/if/call semantics are validated separately from runtime authority
function/call control-flow and memory-effect summaries are explicit IR properties; call-site constraints can refine potential effects
potential side effects can be represented in function types and inferred compositionally

adversarial_check.counterhypothesis: A static effect declaration or transitive function effect summary can itself serve as execution authority, so a separate runtime permit is unnecessary.
adversarial_check.test: Execute an effectful wrapper with valid static effect closure but without runtime permit.
adversarial_check.result: REJECTED_BY_CANDIDATE_RUNTIME: EffectDenied; same call succeeds only when external permit contains log.write.

refinement: Keep control-flow/effect semantics in canonical typed IR, but separate potential-effect identity from effect authority. Recursion/re-entry may preserve semantic dependency identity; delayed effects require fresh external permit/capability validation.
falsifier: A production ClayCode compiler/runtime on target Ubuntu that safely executes the mandatory app/FRANK suite with no false allow/deny while collapsing effect summary and authority into one mechanism would refute the need for this separation.
